chat_prefill.about: Inference on chat prompts: batch 1-8, prompt length log-normal (median 48 tokens) up to the 256-token block

llama_prefill.about: The same request mix on a Llama-style model (RoPE table sliced to the length, grouped-query attention)

greedy_decode.about: Generation without a KV cache: one sequence grows by one token per step from a 16-token prompt

padded_encoder.about: Embedding requests padded to the longest text in the batch: batch 4-32, padding mask

train_variable_length.about: Training steps (forward, loss, backward, AdamW) on batches of 8 sequences whose length varies per batch

rows.about: Causal multi-head self-attention where num_heads is an int argument that sets head_dim = d // num_heads, the -1 in the reshapes and the score scale, and the causal mask is built from the sequence length (including length 1).
ViT patch embedding that crops images to h // 4 * 4 by w // 4 * 4, so odd sizes share a grid with smaller ones, and slices the position table to gh * gw + 1 rows computed from both image sizes.

Sliding-window pooling where the int window unrolls a Python loop and sets the frame count t - window + 1, and the int stride subsamples frames to ceil(n / stride) (including window == t and stride larger than n).
Masked mean pooling after x[:, :16] (an end that runs past short sequences) and a Python branch that pads only when the sequence is shorter than 16, with valid positions taken from per-row lengths.
Shifted language-model loss whose logits[:, :-1] and targets[:, 1:] give t - 1 rows (down to one), whose vocabulary size feeds reshape(-1, v), and whose two inputs must agree on batch and length.

Cross-attention pooling whose second squeeze(1) drops the query axis only when there is exactly one query (so the output rank depends on that size), with a scale whose batch is sometimes 1 and broadcasts and a memory that is sometimes length 1.

Partial rotary embedding that rotates the first 2 * (head_dim // 4) channels and passes the rest through (head_dim 6, 12, 18 leave odd remainders), with an int offset that sets the positions for KV-cache decoding at length 1.

Layout round trip (NCHW -> tokens -> NCHW) followed by a Python branch on h * w > 64 that crops odd edges and max-pools 2x2 before the global mean, so the decision depends on the product of two sizes (8x8 = 64 does not pool, 8x9 does).

Sliding-window KV-cache attention that keeps the last window + tq - 1 keys with a negative slice that may reach past the start (empty or short caches), and builds the mask from positions offset by length - tq.

Embedding plus causal transformer block in eval mode whose positions come from arange(t), with a Python branch on t > 32 that mean-pools only every other token (ceil(t / 2) of them, 33 vs 32 is the edge).
ViT patch embedding with 2D sin-cos positions; images over 1024 pixels are 2x2-pooled first (Python branch on h*w, boundary at 32x32 vs 33x32), and odd sizes are floor-cropped to the patch grid.
Causal multi-head self-attention whose head count is an int argument: it sets the reshape and the 1/sqrt(head_dim) scale, and sequence length 1 makes the causal mask 1x1.

Cumsum-based moving average with window k: output length t-k+1 comes from c[:, k:] - c[:, :-k], and a Python branch returns a (B, 1) mean instead when the series is shorter than the window (t == k vs t == k-1).

Masked label-smoothed cross entropy: the smoothing mass eps/V and the one-hot both depend on the vocabulary size V (including V=1), logits are flattened with reshape(-1, V), and the smoothing int sets eps.

NHWC->NCHW space-to-depth preprocessing: mean/std are sometimes (1,) and broadcast, a Python branch expands 1-channel images to 3, h and w are floor-cropped to multiples of the int factor r, and the channel count comes from a -1 reshape.

Embedding-bag text classifier that truncates with tokens[:, :max_len]: max_len is sometimes larger than the sequence, so the real length is min(T, max_len), and pooling divides by a clamped count of non-pad tokens.

RoPE for KV-cache decoding with grouped-query keys: the int offset changes only values (absolute positions, so it must not be baked in), the rotation splits the head dim at d//2, q is scaled by d**-0.5, and keys are repeated Hq//Hk times (Hk sometimes 1 or equal to Hq).
GRU unrolled with a Python loop over x.shape[1], so the traced graph has one step per time step (T=6 vs 7 vs 5 vs 1 must not share a graph), with a length mask freezing finished sequences.

Symmetric CLIP loss with K captions per image: K is computed as txt rows // img rows (image and text batch sizes must agree up to K), batch size 1 gives a 1x1 logit matrix, and logit_scale is sometimes () and sometimes (1,).
Windowed attention that pads T up to a multiple of the int window (pad = (w - T % w) % w, zero when T divides), masks the padded keys, and slices the padding off with [:, :T].
